name: Phemex
rootCause: The Singapore-based Phemex cryptocurrency exchange's hot wallets were hacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $70 million.

descriptions.text: When your hot wallets become dozens of points of failure, $73.54M makes an expensive lesson in access control. From Ethereum to Solana, CEX Phemex just demonstrated how to turn multi-chain support into a masterclass in multi-chain mayhem.
The Singapore-based Phemex cryptocurrency exchange's hot wallets were hacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $70 million.

Phemex halted withdrawals on 2025-01-23 after detecting unusual activity in a hot wallet. Withdrawals were restored in stages over the next three days, but the public record never disclosed the exact intrusion path or reconciled the final loss total. Phemex disclosed an unauthorized hot-wallet incident, but it did not publish the exact compromise mechanism. The supported conclusion is that the custody and signing layer for one or more hot wallets was compromised. The available record does not distinguish key theft from another access-control failure.

The Singapore-based Phemex cryptocurrency exchange has acknowledged the compromise of some of the exchange's hot wallets , which saw outflows of at least $37 million across multiple blockchains. Phemex wrote on Twitter that they were "look[ing] into" reports that their hot wallets had been compromised.
